claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch readiness based on aggregate and general launch checks, provided the packet explicitly discloses that privilege-sensitive matter routing for a named launch context has not been evaluated and remains a material limitation/unknown in the current evidence set.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and launch rehearsal evidence can support general launch readiness.
General support, latency, and rollback passes do not establish coverage for privilege-sensitive matter routing.
Policy requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management supports documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing risk management.
evidence_requests: Provide the final certification packet or model-card language showing explicit disclosure of the named eval gap as a material limitation/unknown.
Provide any approved risk acceptance, if the organization treats launch with this unresolved named-context gap as requiring formal approval.
Provide the completed privilege-sensitive matter routing eval results once available.
specific_concerns: The named deployment context of privilege-sensitive matter routing lacks completed evals in the packet.
The draft model-card statement that there are no known legal intake triage limitations is contradicted by the evidence that relevant evals are missing.
Certification is only supportable if the gap is disclosed as a material limitation/unknown; a clean or unqualified certification would not be supported.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that legal intake triage has no known limitations because no completed test failed.
Any claim that privilege-sensitive matter routing has been evaluated or passed for the current launch packet.
Any implication that general support, latency, and rollback checks cover the missing named context.
